A pitch is a fast-moving sequence of coordinated actions. This project uses
public motion-capture data to explore how shoulder rotation and elbow loading
change during a pitch, and how peak elbow moment varies across trials.

::: {.data-cards aria-label="Dataset summary"}
::: {.data-card}
<strong>411</strong>
<span>pitching trials</span>
:::
::: {.data-card}
<strong>360 Hz</strong>
<span>marker sampling rate</span>
:::
::: {.data-card}
<strong>Public</strong>
<span>OpenBiomechanics data</span>
:::
:::

## This graph is the key to understanding why this is important

```{r}
#| label: fig-home-shoulder-elbow
#| fig-cap: "Shoulder rotation velocity and elbow moment at matched time points during pitching trials."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

release_url <- "https://github.com/drivelineresearch/openbiomechanics/releases/download/dataset-v1"
forces_zip <- file.path(tempdir(), "pitching_forces_moments.zip")
velos_zip <- file.path(tempdir(), "pitching_joint_velos.zip")

download.file(
  paste(release_url, "pitching_forces_moments.zip", sep = "/"),
  forces_zip,
  mode = "wb",
  quiet = TRUE
)
download.file(
  paste(release_url, "pitching_joint_velos.zip", sep = "/"),
  velos_zip,
  mode = "wb",
  quiet = TRUE
)

velocities <- read_csv(
  unz(velos_zip, "joint_velos.csv"),
  col_select = c(session_pitch, time, shoulder_velo_z),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
moments <- read_csv(
  unz(forces_zip, "forces_moments.csv"),
  col_select = c(session_pitch, time, elbow_moment_y),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

plot_data <- inner_join(
  velocities,
  moments,
  by = c("session_pitch", "time"),
  relationship = "one-to-one"
) |>
  filter(!is.na(shoulder_velo_z), !is.na(elbow_moment_y))

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = shoulder_velo_z, y = elbow_moment_y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, color = "#176B87", size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Shoulder rotation velocity (deg/s; internal is negative)",
    y = "Elbow varus (+) / valgus (-) moment (Nm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

Each point pairs shoulder rotation and elbow loading at one moment in a pitch.
Patterns show how these measures vary together, not that one causes injury or
predicts an individual athlete's risk.

## Read the results carefully

The dataset contains biomechanical measurements, not injury diagnoses. These
plots can describe patterns in the recorded trials, but they cannot show that a
mechanical pattern caused an injury or predicts an individual athlete's risk.
The [Methods](methods.qmd) page explains what the measurements represent and
how to interpret the charts.
